1.title: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation. This module covers exam orientation and the course map. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What the exam is: sixty-three items, one hundred twenty minutes, a scaled score of seven hundred twenty to pass. The seven domains, their weights and the thirty-eight objectives behind them. The minimally qualified candidate the exam is written for. The architect decision rules that explain most correct answers. How the course is built and how to use it.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lumen Advisory
1.text: Our running case is Lumen Advisory. Lumen Advisory. Throughout the course you follow Lumen Advisory, a fictional consultancy. Its architects design Claude solutions for clients in banking, healthcare, retail and government. Each module solves one architecture problem for a client; the questions use the same style as the exam.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance
1.text: The Exam at a Glance. The figure shows this: The C C A R P exam at a glance: sixty-three items, one hundred twenty minutes, scaled score one hundred to one thousand with seven hundred twenty to pass, seven domains, U S D one hundred seventy-five, valid twelve months.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Credential or code. Claude Architect to Professional or C C A R P. Items. sixty-three, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select. Time. one hundred twenty minutes (about one minute fifty-four seconds per item). Passing score. seven hundred twenty on a scaled range of one hundred to one thousand (criterion-referenced: a fixed standard, not a ranking). Fee. U S D one hundred seventy-five per attempt. Delivery. Proctored by Pearson V U E: online or at a test center. Validity. twelve months from the date the credential is awarded; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Retakes. Wait fourteen days after the first failed attempt, thirty after the second, ninety after the third; at most four attempts in a rolling twelve months; limits are per exam. Prerequisites. None are required; recommended: three plus years in systems architecture or platform engineering and six plus months with Claude or comparable L L M (large language model) systems in production. Score report. Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (domain figures do not decide pass or fail). Exam tip: For a multiple-response item the stem says how many answers to select: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

1.title: The Seven Domains
1.text: The Seven Domains. The figure shows this: Domain weights: D three Integration nineteen, D one Solution Design and Architecture seventeen, D four Evaluation Testing and Optimization sixteen, D five Governance Safety and Risk fourteen, D six Stakeholder Communication and Lifecycle fourteen, D two Models Prompting and Context thirteen, D seven Developer Productivity seven.

1.title: The Seven Domains, continued
1.text: The Seven Domains, continued. D three Integration. Weight: nineteen percent. What it asks you to do: Spot tool bloat and security gaps; trade accuracy against latency; design R A G; choose M C P (Model Context Protocol), A P I (application programming interface) or C L I (command-line interface) or agent-to-agent; observe at scale. Modules: seven to ten. D one Solution Design and Architecture. Weight: seventeen percent. What it asks you to do: Turn business problems into architectures; pick workflow, agentic or augmented-L L M patterns; design multi-agent systems; decompose. Modules: one to three. D four Evaluation, Testing and Optimization. Weight: sixteen percent. What it asks you to do: Define metrics and datasets; A or B test; diagnose; optimize cost, latency, tokens; monitor. Modules: eleven, twelve. D five Governance, Safety and Risk. Weight: fourteen percent. What it asks you to do: Guardrails, failure modes, human review, G D P R, H I P A A, Fed R A M P, ethics. Modules: thirteen, fourteen.

1.title: The Seven Domains, continued
1.text: The Seven Domains, continued. D six Stakeholder Communication and Lifecycle. Weight: fourteen percent. What it asks you to do: Discovery, communicating trade-offs, S L A s (service level agreement), documentation, lifecycle phases. Modules: fifteen, sixteen. D two Claude Models, Prompting and Context. Weight: thirteen percent. What it asks you to do: Model trade-offs, system prompts, prompting techniques, context and token management, reuse. Modules: four to six. D seven Developer Productivity and Operational Enablement. Weight: seven percent. What it asks you to do: Configure Claude Code for teams, A I-assisted workflows, debugging and operations. Modules: seventeen. Of sixty-three items, about twelve come from D three, eleven from D one, ten from D four, nine each from D five and D six, eight from D two and four to five from D seven.

1.title: The Seven Domains, continued
1.text: The Seven Domains, continued. Weights are the approximate share of scored items. Items are written against the thirty-eight objectives listed in the guide. Study order by value: D three and D one first (over a third together), then D four, D five, D six and D two; D seven is the smallest. Exam tip: No domain is negligible except D seven at seven percent. Integration is the largest, so give it the most practice.

1.title: The Minimally Qualified Candidate
1.text: The Minimally Qualified Candidate. The minimally qualified candidate (M Q C) can. translate business requirements into scalable, secure, reliable architectures. design end-to-end systems: prompt and context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (R A G), A P I integration, orchestration and evaluation. weigh trade-offs among cost, latency, performance, safety and maintainability. integrate Claude into production systems with A P I s, orchestration tools and data pipelines. build in evaluation, monitoring, security, compliance and governance. communicate architectural decisions to engineers, legal and executives.

1.title: The Minimally Qualified Candidate, continued
1.text: The Minimally Qualified Candidate, continued. The figure shows this: The minimally qualified candidate designs, prompts, integrates, evaluates, governs, communicates and enables teams on Claude solutions.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward. Most items describe a requirement or a failure and ask for the best design choice. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Each later module shows them at work.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. one. Rule: Start with the simplest pattern that meets the need (single call, then workflow, then agent). Typical wrong answers: An agent or multi-agent system for a fixed task. two. Rule: Remove risk at the source: least privilege means removing capabilities, not logging them. Typical wrong answers: Adding logging or a confirmation instead of removing the tool. three. Rule: Cache the stable prefix; put static content before dynamic content. Typical wrong answers: Truncating needed context or shrinking the model blindly. four. Rule: Match the model to the task and prove it with evals. Typical wrong answers: "Always the largest" or "always the smallest".

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. five. Rule: Retrieve only what is needed: tool search, progressive discovery, R A G for large knowledge, full context for small. Typical wrong answers: Loading every tool and document up front. six. Rule: Investigate the first place the symptom points: confident wrong answers after a refresh point to retrieval. Typical wrong answers: Blaming silent model changes. seven. Rule: Measure before and after with defined metrics, datasets and controlled comparisons. Typical wrong answers: Judging by a few impressions. eight. Rule: Keep humans in the loop for irreversible or high-risk actions, and enforce rules in code. Typical wrong answers: Stronger prompt wording.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. nine. Rule: Meet the regime with the right platform and contract (B A A, Z D R, data residency, Gov Cloud). Typical wrong answers: Assuming any A P I route is compliant. ten. Rule: Communicate trade-offs, assumptions and S L A s and document decisions. Typical wrong answers: Promising certainty or hiding limits. Exam tip: When two options both work, prefer the one that is simple, least-privileged, measured, cost-aware and compliant.

1.title: How to Use This Course
1.text: How to Use This Course. Order: read modules one to seventeen in order (they follow the domains), then module eighteen (recap) and nineteen (technique). Each module has the objectives it covers, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, scenario questions with explanations and a Quick Reference Card. Build one end-to-end solution. The guide recommends building and operating at least one Claude solution with R A G, evaluation and observability. Product details change fast. Boxes marked show current behavior. On the exam, answer by the principle and check the official documentation for current details.

1.title: How to Use This Course, continued
1.text: How to Use This Course, continued. Independence. This course is independent study material; it is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Anthropic or Pearson V U E. Read the official exam guide, the Certification Terms and Conditions and the Exam Policy before you register.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: C C A R P; sixty-three items; one hundred twenty min; pass seven hundred twenty of one thousand; U S D one hundred seventy-five; valid twelve months. Domains: D three nineteen, D one seventeen, D four sixteen, D five fourteen, D six fourteen, D two thirteen, D seven seven. Objectives: thirty-eight in all. Prerequisites: None required; three plus years architecture and six plus months Claude recommended. Retakes: fourteen, thirty, ninety days; max four per rolling twelve months. Ten rules: Simplest pattern, remove risk at the source, cache the stable prefix, match model to task, retrieve only what is needed, investigate the first symptom, measure, humans in the loop, right platform for the regime, communicate trade-offs. In the next module, we continue the course.
